raw_response:
*[reasoning in my own voice]*

Ai, another year. My back don't work like it used to, but cotton is what I know. Forty-five years on these nine mu, my father grew cotton here, now me. Don't know no other way.

The land is already plowed — my nephew's boy came through with his tractor last month, cost me maybe 40 yuan a mu, cheaper than doing it myself with the donkey like the old days. This week I'll lay down the plastic mulch and get the seed in. Around Grain Rain (谷雨) is when my father always said, around April 20, when the ground stays warm at night. If I plant too early and a cold snap comes, the seedlings yellow out and I'm buying seed again. Waited this long, no sense rushing.

For seed, I'll get the Bt kind from the seed shop in town — everyone uses it now, the bollworm don't eat it so bad. One small bag does about a mu. Costs more than the old seed we used to save, but you save on spray so it evens out. My neighbor Old Wang tried a cheap one two years back, got eaten alive. I'm not trying that.

For fertilizer, I do what I always do: one bag of compound per mu before planting, mixed in when I lay the mulch. That's 50 jin — no wait, 50 kilo, one sack. The 15-15-15 kind. Then at flowering when the plants are about this tall *[gestures]*, I'll sprinkle some urea between the rows, maybe half a sack per mu, and water it in. Any more than that and the plants grow tall and leafy but the bolls don't fill — I learned that the hard way about ten years ago, wasted good money. My wife scolded me for a month.

Water — I have the well, shared with three other families. I'll water once at squaring if it don't rain, again at boll-filling. Twice usually enough for our sandy ground. Electricity for the pump is the killer, but cotton without water is just sticks.

Spray — can't skip. Even with Bt cotton, the aphids come, and the spider mites if it's dry. Three, maybe four times through the summer. I buy whatever the shop recommends, they know my land.

Picking — that's the family. My wife, me, my son's wife when she's not at the market. Nine mu, maybe three or four rounds of picking from end of August to October. Don't hire no one, can't afford it. Kids grown, no help there.

What will I get? If the weather is normal, maybe 250 kilo of seed cotton per mu, sell at maybe 3 yuan per jin for the picked stuff. Last year was dry in August, only got 220. Year before was good, 280. You never know. I budget for the bad year.
